According to a statement from the Turkish Embassy in Mogadishu, the meeting focused on the common will to further enhance bilateral ties and friendly human connections. The discussions covered ongoing cooperation projects in energy, infrastructure, fisheries, security, health, education, space, and connectivity. The embassy thanked Prime Minister Barre for his reception and his support for Türkiye-Somalia friendship. The Prime Minister’s Office has previously expressed gratitude for Ankara’s role in rebuilding the Somali Armed Forces and modernising government institutions, highlighting the security dimension of the partnership [citation:10]. A Comprehensive Diplomatic Tour Wednesday’s meeting with the Prime Minister is part of a broader diplomatic tour Ambassador Alkan has undertaken since arriving in Mogadishu in September 2026. His engagement with Somali leadership has been extensive, signaling Ankara’s intent to maintain its deep footprint in the country. Ambassador Alkan began his tenure by presenting his credentials to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in early October, marking the start of his mission during the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the credentials ceremony . He also visited the spaceport facility under construction in Warsheikh district, inspecting progress on a project that underscores the strategic and technological depth of the relationship, as detailed in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the visit . Beyond the executive branch, Alkan has engaged with security leadership. He recently met with the Somali Police Commissioner, Brigadier General Asad Osman Abdullahi, to discuss enhancing bilateral cooperation in the security sector, with a particular emphasis on advancing training programs and building the capacity of the Somali Police Force, especially the elite Haramcad unit, as noted in FTL Somalia’s coverage of police cooperation . In previous months, his predecessor, Alper Aktaş, held similar talks with the National Security Advisor and the Defence Minister, maintaining a consistent line of communication between Ankara and Mogadishu’s security apparatus. His diplomatic activity also extends to the legislative and informational branches. In May, the Turkish Embassy engaged with the Ministry of Information to develop frameworks for media modernization and cross-cultural exchange, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the information ministry talks . The Strategic Depth and Its Complications Türkiye’s relationship with Somalia is among the most comprehensive of any external actor. It spans humanitarian aid, infrastructure development, military training, and economic investment. Turkish firms operate Mogadishu’s port and airport, and the 2024 defense agreement has given Ankara a significant role in Somalia’s maritime security. However, this deepening engagement has not been without controversy. The federal government’s political opponents, including former South West State President Abdiaziz Laftagareen, have accused Türkiye of enabling a “clan-based agenda” through its military support, specifically citing F-16 airstrikes in the Baidoa region, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the complaint . The complaint adds a layer of political risk to Ankara’s military presence, entangling it in Somalia’s internal disputes. Critical Note Ambassador Alkan’s meeting with Prime Minister Barre is a routine diplomatic engagement, but the breadth of sectors discussed, from energy and fisheries to space and connectivity, reflects a relationship that has moved far beyond traditional aid. Türkiye is embedded in Somalia’s security architecture, its economic infrastructure, and even its technological ambitions. The diplomatic tour Alkan is conducting is a testament to the institutional depth of the relationship. He is not just meeting with the President and Prime Minister; he is engaging with the police, the information ministry, and visiting strategic projects like the spaceport. This is the behavior of an ambassador whose country has significant, long-term interests to protect. But the partnership’s intensity also carries risks. As the Laftagareen complaint demonstrates, Türkiye’s military role has made it a participant, willing or not, in Somalia’s internal political conflicts. The Somali government values Turkish support, but it also uses it as a shield against domestic and international criticism. The question for Ambassador Alkan is whether he can manage a relationship that is expanding in scope while navigating the political sensitivities that come with such deep involvement. The meeting on Wednesday was a reaffirmation of friendship. The challenge lies in what that friendship requires in practice. Editorial Featured politics SOMALIA Northeastern State: Somalia’s Cornered Frontline Region in the Red Sea Proxy Contest. Last updated: October 23, 2026 3:23 pm Pan African Visions Share SHARE Dr. Abdijalil Hassan* MOGADISHU — A geopolitical map displayed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an October 18 security briefing has thrust Somalia’s newly inaugurated Northeastern State into the center of a widening Red Sea proxy contest, revealing a stark strategic divide between the fledgling federal member state and the UAE and Israel-aligned regions of Somaliland and Puntland. The map, which Netanyahu presented while outlining Israel’s updated national security doctrine ahead of elections, color-codes Somaliland and Puntland in light blue as part of a purported “Hexagon Alliance” friendly to Israel and the United Arab Emirates. The rest of Somalia, including the separately identified Northeastern State appears in light green under the “Sunni Diamond” grouping, comprising Türkiye, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. While the graphic was originally produced by researchers at Germany’s Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung and represents an analytical assessment of alignments rather than formal treaty commitments, its display by Netanyahu has given it unmistakable political weight. For the Northeastern State, the classification is both a strategic confirmation and a vulnerability. Inaugurated in January 2026 with the backing of the Somali federal government, the state, centered on Las Anod was created from territory previously claimed by Somaliland and Puntland, both of which have rejected the new administration and its federal alignment. the Northeastern State’s forces defeated their adversaries in late fighting and took control of contested areas that its neighbors have long claimed. That battlefield outcome has strengthened popular backing for the new federal member state among residents who view it as a long-overdue institutional answer to decades of instability and overlapping claims. the State now finds itself geographically cornered between two regions that are not only hostile to its existence but are now explicitly linked on Netanyahu’s map to the Israel-UAE strategic orbit. The map’s implications extend beyond symbolism. Somaliland has received significant diplomatic and security backing from both the UAE and Israel, particularly following Israel’s December 2025 recognition of Somaliland as an “independent state”, a move Somali Federal Republic rejected as a violation of its sovereignty. Puntland, though still a federal member state, has developed deep economic and security ties with the UAE, including involvement in the operation of Bosaso port and cooperation in military training. Together, the two regions form a de facto corridor of Emirati and Israeli influence along the Gulf of Aden, directly abutting the Northeastern State’s territory. By contrast, the Northeastern State is firmly anchored in the Sunni Diamond camp. Its federal patrons Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan have moved decisively to institutionalize their security relationship with Somalia. In August 2026, the three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, committing to collective deterrence in which an armed attack against one would be treated as an attack against all. Somalia’s defense ministry welcomed the pact as a strategic partnership capable of addressing shared security challenges. Pakistan has separately deepened defense cooperation with Mogadishu, including discussions on rebuilding the Somali Air Force and reported interest in JF-17 fighter aircraft, while Saudi Arabia signed a military cooperation memorandum with Somalia in February 2026. Egypt and Qatar have also been identified as federal allies supporting the Northeastern State’s inauguration as a counterweight to Emirati influence. Yet the presence of powerful patrons does not erase the Northeastern State’s immediate predicament. It is a new, institutionally fragile administration surrounded by rivals with established foreign backers, and its adversaries have shown no inclination to accept its legitimacy. Somaliland’s leadership has framed the state’s creation as a partition of its claimed territory; Puntland has withdrawn its recognition of the federal government altogether and joined an anti-Mogadishu political coalition. The map Netanyahu displayed did not create these tensions, but it has clarified the lines along which they are likely to escalate: the Northeastern State is not merely a domestic federal experiment but a frontline node in the competition between the Israel-UAE axis and the Türkiye-Saudi-Pakistan constellation. For the Northeastern State’s allies, the message is urgent. The state’s survival depends on tangible support, security guarantees, reconstruction funding, and diplomatic cover from Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, whose own strategic interests in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden increasingly converge on preventing the further expansion of Emirati and Israeli influence along Somalia’s northern coast. The Mecca defense pact provides a framework, but frameworks alone do not secure borders. If the Sunni Diamond powers intend to hold the line in northern Somalia, the cornered Northeastern State will need more than a color on a map. *Dr. Abdijalil Hassan ia a former lecturer at East Africa University, provides expert analysis on conflict dynamics across the Horn of Africa. Dowladda Federaalka Galmudug Hiiraan News Jubaland News Koonfur Galbeed SSC Somaliland Follow us Search News Somalia Somalia faces risk of mass displacement as floods threaten hundreds of thousands Posted by: Horseed Staff About 874,000 people in Somalia could be forced from their homes over the next three months as heavy rainfall and rising river levels increase the risk of widespread flooding, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned. 23 October, 2026 Share Tweet The warning comes as communities across the country continue to recover from prolonged drought and repeated displacement. The IOM said on Wednesday that the risk of flooding between October and December could leave hundreds of thousands of people without homes or livelihoods. The situation is being compounded by forecasts of above-average rainfall, as El Niño conditions are expected to intensify. “We are looking at the possibility of hundreds of thousands of people losing their homes in just a matter of weeks,” said Manuel Marques Pereira, the IOM’s chief of mission in Somalia. “Many of these families have already been displaced before and have very little left to fall back on.” Mr Marques Pereira said there was still an opportunity to reduce the impact of the floods, but warned that time was running out. “We urgently need funding to help people protect their homes and livelihoods, reach safer ground where necessary, and avoid another cycle of displacement,” he said. The warning has raised concerns over the prospect of people being forced to undertake dangerous journeys in search of safety, including across borders and by sea. Humanitarian organisations have also warned that climate-related disasters could further deepen Somalia’s existing humanitarian crisis, with the risk of severe food shortages and famine. Somalia has faced repeated droughts, floods and displacement in recent years, placing additional pressure on communities already struggling with limited access to food, water and basic services. El Niño occurs when sea surface temperatures rise in parts of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean. The phenomenon can disrupt atmospheric circulation and influence weather patterns around the world. Its effects vary from region to region. In some areas it can contribute to severe drought, while in others it can bring heavier rainfall and an increased risk of flooding. For Somalia, the immediate concern is that further flooding could force already vulnerable communities from their homes once again, adding to a cycle of displacement that humanitarian agencies are struggling to address. somalia.title: China, Djibouti oppose recognition of Somaliland, back Somalia - Anadolu Ajansı
somalia.summary: China and Djibouti have jointly expressed their opposition to the recognition of Somaliland, reaffirming their support for Somalia's territorial integrity. This stance was articulated in a statement following discussions between Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Djiboutian Foreign Minister Abdoulkader Houssein Omar in Beijing. The two nations emphasized their commitment to Somalia's sovereignty, explicitly rejecting any diplomatic recognition of Somaliland as an independent entity. They reiterated that Somaliland is an integral part of the Federal Republic of Somalia and condemned any potential collaboration between Somaliland and Taiwan. This declaration comes in the wake of Israel's recognition of Somaliland as an independent state in December 2025, which sparked backlash from Somalia and other nations. Somaliland has operated as a de facto independent region since declaring independence from Somalia in 1991, yet it has not received international recognition. Somalia views any direct agreements made by Somaliland with foreign entities as infringements on its sovereignty.

Studies show the full implementation of the AfCFTA would increase intra-African trade by 52 percent or by $450 billion by 2035, according to the World Bank. Photo credit: File | NMG By Luke Anami Correspondent in Nairobi, Kenya Nation Media Group Thank you for reading businessdailyafrica.com Show plans Somalia has officially become the 50th State Party to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), completing a series of protocol steps needed to be a part of commercial framework. Mogadishu formally deposited its instrument of ratification at the African Union headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on September 4 last month but details of formal membership were confirmed this week. AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene told an audience at the official opening of this year’s 26th Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) Summit in Harare, Zimbabwe that Somalia will now start enjoying full rights in the deal. Related East Africa PRIME Somalia assesses EAC membership benefits, two years on Oct 18 - 4 min read Africa PRIME Inside EAC, Comesa plan to cut paperwork, fees on cross-border trade Oct 21 - 4 min read The move grants Somali businesses and investors preferential access to a continental market of over 1.4 billion consumers. “In terms of implementation of the AfCFTA, your excellences, as we speak today, 54 members of the African Union have signed the agreement establishing the AfCFTA,” said Mene. “50 members of the African Union have ratified it. Somalia is the most recent member of the African Union to ratify the agreement establishing the AfCFTA. We congratulate Somalia for being the 50th state party to the AfCFTA, which further strengthens Comesa's contribution to continental trade.” Somalia’s participation adds further momentum to the collective effort to deepen regional value chains, expand trade and build a more integrated and prosperous Africa. It joined the East African Community at the end of 2024, after also receiving formal nod on debt forgiveness by a various international lenders including the World Bank. Gamal Mohamed Hassan, Somalia’s Minister for Commerce and Industry, submitted the instrument of ratification in September following its approval by Parliament and presidential assent from President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. "Somalia's participation in the AfCFTA will create greater opportunities for local enterprises to access continental markets, attract foreign investment, diversify exports and participate effectively in regional value chains, supporting the country's broader economic development," said Hassan on Thursday. The government viewed the agreement as a platform to accelerate industrialisation, attract investment and drive economic growth, adding that the ministry would work closely with the private sector to maximise opportunities arising from membership. The ministry said its next priorities include aligning Somalia's tariff schedules with AfCFTA commitments, developing the required trade instruments and conducting nationwide outreach to help businesses, exporters, cooperatives and small and medium-sized enterprises prepare for implementation. The AfCFTA Secretariat welcomed Somalia and looks forward to supporting the country as it advances domestic implementation and creates opportunities for the Somali private sector to participate effectively in intra-African trade. Somalia is a member of the East African Community as well as Comesa, both of which are regional blocs that serve as the main anchors for an effective AfCFTA. “Our regional economic communities are the building blocks of the continental market. And in this regard, we value the collaboration with Comesa and other regional economic communities,” said Mene. Among the 21 member states of Comesa, the vast majority have ratified the agreement, including Kenya, Rwanda, Djibouti, Eswatini, Uganda, Egypt, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe, Tunisia, Mauritius, Malawi, Zambia, Burundi, Seychelles, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Comoros, Madagascar and, most recently, Somalia. The 50 ratifying nations include Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, Niger and Chad in the initial group, followed by a broad coalition across the continent, with Comoros, Mozambique, Liberia, Madagascar and Somalia among the most recent members. The AfCFTA aims to boost intra-African trade by lowering trade barriers and establishing a unified framework for the seamless movement of goods and services across the continent. تصل معركة البقاء في دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027 إلى مرحلة حاسمة في عطلة نهاية هذا الأسبوع؛ إذ تواجه أندية أفريقية عريقة خطر الإقصاء المبكر، بينما تسعى فرق طموحة لتحقيق مفاجآت مدوية وحجز مقاعدها في دور المجموعات. يتعين على أندية الترجي التونسي (بطل أفريقيا أربع مرات)، ومولودية الجزائر، وبترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي، تعويض خسائرها المؤلمة في مباريات الذهاب، وذلك خلال جولة الإياب من الدور التمهيدي الثاني، التي تُقام 15 مباراة منها في الفترة ما بين الجمعة 23 أكتوبر والأحد 25 أكتوبر 2026. كما يواجه حامل اللقب، ماميلودي صنداونز، اختباراً مصيرياً بعد تعادله سلبياً في مباراة الذهاب أمام فريق "ويليتي" الأنغولي، في حين يتوجب على تي بي مازيمبي -الفائز باللقب خمس مرات- تجاوز عقبة النادي الأفريقي التونسي للحفاظ على آماله القارية. وتأتي هذه الجولة الحاسمة بعد تأهل نادي "يانغ أفريكانز" التنزاني، الذي أصبح أول فريق يضمن مقعداً في دور المجموعات، عقب فوزه يوم الأربعاء على "سي إف إف إيه" ( CFFA ) من مدغشقر بنتيجة 4-1، ليحسم المواجهة لصالحه بنتيجة إجمالية بلغت 8-1. ومع تأهل "يانغ أفريكانز" بالفعل، تتبقى 15 مقعداً شاغراً في دور المجموعات، الذي من المقرر أن ينطلق في أواخر شهر نوفمبر. ومن بين أكثر المواجهات إثارة، يسعى الترجي التونسي لإنقاذ مسيرته في البطولة عندما يستضيف فريق "السويحلي" الليبي يوم السبت؛ حيث يمتلك الفريق الليبي أفضلية الفوز ذهاباً بنتيجة 1-0، ولا يفصله سوى 90 دقيقة عن تحقيق أحد أكبر الإنجازات في تاريخه القاري. وفي مواجهة صعبة أخرى، يستقبل مولودية الجزائر فريق "رينجرز إنترناشيونال" النيجيري يوم الجمعة، وهو مطالب بتعويض خسارته ذهاباً بهدفين نظيفين. وفي سياق مشابه، يواجه بترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي تحدياً كبيراً عند استضافته لفريق "سكوتلاند إف سي" الزيمبابوي، بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب بخسارة الفريق الأنغولي بهدفين دون رد. يواجه فريق "صنداونز" اختباراً صعباً عندما يستضيف "ويليتي" في بريتوريا، وذلك بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب في أنغولا بالتعادل السلبي (0-0). وفي تونس، تُقام مواجهة قوية أخرى يوم الأحد، حيث يستضيف "النادي الأفريقي" فريق "تي ​​بي مازيمبي" -الفائز باللقب الأفريقي خمس مرات- بعد أن تعادل الفريقان بنتيجة (1-1) في لوبومباشي. وبينما تواجه بعض الأندية العريقة ضغوطاً كبيرة، تسعى أندية أخرى لحسم تأهلها رسمياً بعد تقديمها أداءً قوياً في مباريات الذهاب. يدخل فريق "نهضة بركان" المغربي مباراة الإياب على أرضه يوم السبت متسلحاً بتقدمه (2-0) على "ستار سبورت أكاديمي" من سيراليون، بينما يسعى "الهلال" السوداني للحفاظ على تقدمه بنفس النتيجة أمام "بن سيداما " الإثيوبي يوم الأحد. كما يتمتع فريق "كولومب سبورتيف" الكاميروني بوضع مريح بعد تحقيقه فوزاً لافتاً خارج أرضه بنتيجة (2-0) على "تونغيث" السنغالي، مما يجعله على أعتاب التأهل لدور المجموعات. وقد تشهد المرحلة المقبلة حضوراً مزدوجاً لتنزانيا؛ إذ يُعد فريق "سيمبا" الأقرب للانضمام إلى "يانغ أفريكانز" بعد تحقيقه فوزاً ساحقاً بنتيجة (6-1) خارج دياره على "15 دي أغوستو" من غينيا الاستوائية يوم الأربعاء. وفي مصر، يسعى كل من "بيراميدز" و"الزمالك" لحسم التأهل على أرضهما يوم السبت، بعد أن حقق كلاهما الفوز بنتيجة (1-0) خارج الديار في جولة الذهاب، أمام "المريخ بنتيو" من جنوب السودان و"الجيش" الرواندي على التوالي. ويضع فريق "أورلاندو بايرتس" الجنوب أفريقي نفسه في موقف جيد بعد فوزه (1-0) خارج ملعبه على "أفريكان ستارز" الناميبي، رغم أنه سيحتاج إلى تقديم أداء منضبط مجدداً في مباراة الإياب. وفي سياق آخر، يأمل فريق "أسيك ميموزا" الإيفواري في استغلال عاملي الأرض والجمهور أمام "المغرب الفاسي" المغربي، بعد تعادلهما (1-1) في لقاء الذهاب. أما فريق "هورويا" الغيني فيسافر لمواجهة "المريخ" السوداني وهو متقدم بفارق ضئيل (1-0)، في حين يتعين على "نواذيبو" الموريتاني تعويض خسارته ذهاباً (2-1) أمام "سان بيدرو" الإيفواري. تشير الفوارق الضئيلة في العديد من هذه المواجهات إلى أن نتائج معارك التأهل لا تزال غير محسومة، مع احتمالية حدوث المزيد من المفاجآت في ظل سعي الأندية المستمر للبقاء في دائرة المنافسة على المجد القاري. وستنضم الأندية الـ 15 المتأهلة إلى فريق "يانغ أفريكانز" في دور المجموعات، الذي يضم 16 فريقاً، ضمن منافسات دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027. دوري أبطال
